correctness.rationale: The exact random hyperplane event is described by two offset intervals with lengths H cos(theta)+w sin(theta) for any hit and [H cos(theta)-w sin(theta)]_+ for an intact full infinite-cylinder section. Direct angular integration gives F_H(w/2), and Cauchy perimeter fixes its normalization. The kernel is strictly convex. Planar zonoid representation and two Jensen applications prove the complete sharp range and equality classes, including strictness for full-dimensional bases; strong convexity proves a width-variance gap. Exact change of variables gives the disk ellipse-eccentricity law and beta limits. The reproducible checker verifies symbolic derivatives, sharp expansions, independent quadrature on symmetric/asymmetric polygons and the conditional CDF. Universal claims rest on the analytic argument, not finite testing.

value.rationale: The probability of observing an untruncated section in an isotropic cross-section experiment is a natural geometric stereological invariant. The result determines a complete all-base fixed-perimeter range, including all noncircular constant-width minimizers, a strict degenerate-segment supremum, and a quantitative width-fluctuation stability inequality. Circular cylinders additionally have an exact conditional ellipticity law with two distinct beta limits and a singular height regime; the statement is a structural classification rather than a routine isolated number.
